exercises.title: Linear inequality
exercises.description: Solve $2x - 3 < 7$ and give the solution set as an interval.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Solve like an equation. The sign only flips when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.

Step 2: Rearrange
$2x < 10$, then $x < 5$.

Step 3: Solution set
$L = (-\infty, 5)$. The $5$ is not included because $<$ is strict.

Step 4: Check
$x = 4$: $8 - 3 = 5 < 7$ ✓. $x = 5$: $10 - 3 = 7 < 7$ ✗ – endpoint excluded.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
Strict inequality → round bracket at the end, $\le$ → square bracket.

exercises.title: The sign flips
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
We divide by a negative number – the sign flips.

Step 2: Divide by $-3$
$x \le -4$.

Step 3: Solution set
$L = (-\infty, -4]$.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
If you don't flip the sign you get $x \ge -4$ – exactly the wrong side. A check with one number reveals this.

exercises.title: Fractions in the inequality
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Multiply by the positive common denominator $6$ – the sign stays.

Step 2: Multiply
$3(x + 1) > 2(x - 1)$.

Step 3: Solve
$3x + 3 > 2x - 2 \Rightarrow x > -5$.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
$L = (-5, \infty)$. Multiplying by a positive number doesn't change the sign.

exercises.title: Interval and inequality
exercises.description: Write as an interval: a) $-1 \le x < 4$, b) $x \le 2$, c) $x > -3$ and $x \le 1$. Write as an inequality: d) $(0, 7]$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Square bracket: endpoint included. Round bracket: endpoint excluded.

Step 3: b)
$(-\infty, 2]$. Next to $\infty$ there is always a round bracket.

Step 4: c)
Both conditions at once: $(-3, 1]$.

Step 5: d)
$0 < x \le 7$.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
The word “and” corresponds to the intersection, “or” to the union.

exercises.title: Computing absolute values
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
The absolute value is the distance from $0$ and never negative. First evaluate the content, then take the absolute value.

Step 3: c)
$|-2| \cdot |5| = 2 \cdot 5 = 10$. We have $|ab| = |a||b|$.

Step 4: d)
$-|-4| = -4$. The minus is OUTSIDE the bars.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
Careful: $|-4|$ and $-|4|$ are different: $4$ versus $-4$.

exercises.title: Simple absolute-value equation
exercises.description: Solve $|x - 3| = 4$ and interpret the result as a distance.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$|x - 3| = 4$ means: $x$ has distance $4$ from $3$.

Step 2: Two cases
$x - 3 = 4$ or $x - 3 = -4$.

Step 4: Interpretation
From $3$, go $4$ to the right or $4$ to the left: $3 + 4 = 7$ and $3 - 4 = -1$.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
If the right-hand side of $|\ldots| = c$ is negative, there is no solution. For $c = 0$ exactly one.

exercises.title: Distance inequality
exercises.description: Determine the solution sets of a) $|x - 5| < 3$ and b) $|x - 5| \ge 3$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$|x - 5| < 3$: all numbers less than $3$ away from $5$.

Step 3: b) Opposite
Distance at least $3$: $x \le 2$ or $x \ge 8$.

Step 4: b) Notation
$L = (-\infty, 2] \cup [8, \infty)$. The endpoints are included because of $\ge$.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
$<$ gives ONE interval around the centre, $>$ gives TWO regions outside.

exercises.title: Simple quadratic inequalities
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Only $x^2$ and a number appear: taking the root means comparing $|x|$.

Step 3: b)
$|x| > 4 \iff x < -4$ or $x > 4$. $L = (-\infty, -4) \cup (4, \infty)$.

Step 4: c)
$x^2 < -1$ is impossible since $x^2 \ge 0$. $L = \emptyset$.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
$x^2 > 16$ does not imply only $x > 4$: $x = -5$ satisfies the inequality too.

exercises.title: Quadratic inequality
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
First find the roots, then decide where the parabola lies below the $x$-axis.

Step 2: Roots
$x^2 - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3)$, so $x = 2$ and $x = 3$.

Step 3: Signs
The parabola opens upwards: between the roots it is negative, outside positive.

Step 4: Solution set
Because of $\le$ the roots are included: $L = [2, 3]$.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
With $\le 0$ or $\ge 0$ the roots belong to the solution, with $<$ or $>$ they don't.

exercises.title: Quadratic inequality, two regions
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Roots, then signs of the upward-opening parabola.

Step 2: Roots
$x^2 - 2x - 8 = (x + 2)(x - 4)$, so $x = -2$ and $x = 4$.

Step 4: Solution set
We need $> 0$: $L = (-\infty, -2) \cup (4, \infty)$.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
Parabola upwards and $> 0$: the OUTER regions. A frequent mistake is writing the solution as the single interval $-2 < x < 4$.

exercises.title: Rational inequality
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
A fraction is $\ge 0$ when numerator and denominator have the same sign – but the denominator must not be $0$.

Step 2: Critical points
Numerator $= 0$ at $x = -1$ (allowed). Denominator $= 0$ at $x = 3$ (forbidden).

Step 4: Solution set
$L = (-\infty, -1] \cup (3, \infty)$. The $-1$ is included (fraction $= 0$), the $3$ is not.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
Zeros of the numerator may belong to the solution for $\ge$, zeros of the denominator never.

exercises.title: Absolute-value inequality with “less than”
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$|u| \le c$ (with $c \ge 0$) means $-c \le u \le c$.

Step 2: Double inequality
$-5 \le 2x - 1 \le 5$.

Step 3: Solve
$+1$: $-4 \le 2x \le 6$, then $:2$: $-2 \le x \le 3$.

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
As a distance: the centre is $x = \frac{1}{2}$, the radius $\frac{5}{2}$. Indeed $\frac{1}{2} \pm \frac{5}{2} = 3$ and $-2$.

exercises.title: Absolute-value inequality with “greater than”
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$|u| > c$ means $u > c$ or $u < -c$ – two regions.

Step 2: Case 1
$x + 2 > 3 \Rightarrow x > 1$.

Step 3: Case 2
$x + 2 < -3 \Rightarrow x < -5$.

Step 4: Solution set
$L = (-\infty, -5) \cup (1, \infty)$.

Step 5: Interpretation
The distance from $x$ to $-2$ should exceed $3$: that holds outside $(-5, 1)$ ✓.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
$|u| > c$ splits into “or”, $|u| < c$ stays “and” (double inequality).

exercises.title: Absolute-value equation with cases
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
The content of the absolute value changes sign at $x = -1$. We distinguish two cases.

Step 2: Case $x \ge -1$
$x + 1 = 2x - 4 \Rightarrow x = 5$. Fits the case assumption $x \ge -1$ ✓.

Step 3: Case $x < -1$
$-(x + 1) = 2x - 4 \Rightarrow -x - 1 = 2x - 4 \Rightarrow x = 1$. This contradicts $x < -1$ ✗.

Step 4: Solution set
$L = \{5\}$.

Step 5: Check
$|5 + 1| = 6$ and $2 \cdot 5 - 4 = 6$ ✓.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
Every solution must fit its case assumption – otherwise it is extraneous.

exercises.title: Checking the triangle inequality
exercises.description: a) Check $|a + b| \le |a| + |b|$ for $a = -4$, $b = 3$. b) When does equality hold? c) Check $\big||a| - |b|\big| \le |a - b|$ for the same numbers.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
We substitute and look for a pattern in the equality case.

Step 3: b) Equality
Example $a = 2$, $b = 5$: $|2 + 5| = 7 = 2 + 5$. Equality holds when $a$ and $b$ have the same sign (or one of them is $0$).

Step 5: Takeaway: What to remember
Geometrically: walking first $a$ and then $b$ covers at most the sum of the distances – a detour can only be longer.

exercises.title: Double inequality
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
A double inequality contains two inequalities that must BOTH hold.

Step 2: Left inequality
$3x - 1 < 2x + 4 \Rightarrow x < 5$.

Step 3: Right inequality
$2x + 4 < 5x + 1 \Rightarrow 3 < 3x \Rightarrow x > 1$.

Step 4: Intersection
$x < 5$ and $x > 1$: $L = (1, 5)$.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
For a chain, “and” applies: intersect the solution sets.

exercises.title: Rational inequality by rearranging
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Bring everything to one side and combine into one fraction, then compare signs of numerator and denominator. Don't multiply by $x + 2$!

Step 2: One side
$\frac{2x - 1}{x + 2} - 1 = \frac{2x - 1 - (x + 2)}{x + 2} = \frac{x - 3}{x + 2} < 0$.

Step 3: Critical points
Numerator $0$ at $x = 3$, denominator $0$ at $x = -2$ (forbidden).

Step 5: Solution set
We need $< 0$: $L = (-2, 3)$. Check: $x = 0$: $-\frac{1}{2} < 1$ ✓; $x = 4$: $\frac{7}{6} < 1$ ✗.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
The bracket around $(x + 2)$ when subtracting is crucial: $-(x + 2) = -x - 2$.

exercises.title: Two absolute values
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
The absolute values switch at $x = 3$ and $x = -1$. Three cases.

Step 2: Case $x < -1$
$-(x - 3) - (x + 1) = -2x + 2 \ge 6 \Rightarrow x \le -2$. Fits: $(-\infty, -2]$.

Step 3: Case $-1 \le x < 3$
$(3 - x) + (x + 1) = 4 \ge 6$ – false. No solution.

Step 4: Case $x \ge 3$
$(x - 3) + (x + 1) = 2x - 2 \ge 6 \Rightarrow x \ge 4$. Fits: $[4, \infty)$.

Step 5: Solution set
$L = (-\infty, -2] \cup [4, \infty)$. Check: $x = 4$: $1 + 5 = 6$ ✓; $x = 0$: $3 + 1 = 4 \ge 6$ ✗.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
Geometrically: the sum of the distances to $3$ and $-1$ is constantly $4$ between the points and grows outside.

exercises.title: Quadratic inequality with a parameter
exercises.description: For which $k$ does $x^2 + kx + 1 > 0$ hold for ALL real $x$?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
The upward-opening parabola lies above the $x$-axis everywhere exactly when it has no root, i.e. the discriminant is negative.

Step 2: Discriminant
$D = k^2 - 4 \cdot 1 \cdot 1 = k^2 - 4$.

Step 3: Condition
$D < 0 \iff k^2 < 4 \iff |k| < 2$.

Step 4: Solution set
$-2 < k < 2$.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
“For all $x$” becomes a condition on the discriminant. $k = \pm 2$ are the borderline cases with one root.

exercises.title: Mean inequalities
exercises.description: Show: a) $a^2 + b^2 \ge 2ab$ for all real $a, b$. b) $\frac{a}{b} + \frac{b}{a} \ge 2$ for $a, b > 0$. c) When does equality hold?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
A square is never negative. That is the basic idea of both proofs.

Step 2: a)
$(a - b)^2 \ge 0 \iff a^2 - 2ab + b^2 \ge 0 \iff a^2 + b^2 \ge 2ab$. $\square$

Step 3: b)
For $a, b > 0$: $\frac{a}{b} + \frac{b}{a} = \frac{a^2 + b^2}{ab} \ge \frac{2ab}{ab} = 2$ (by a) and $ab > 0$). $\square$

Step 4: c) Equality
Exactly when $(a - b)^2 = 0$, i.e. $a = b$.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
When multiplying by $ab$, $ab > 0$ is needed – hence the assumption $a, b > 0$.

exercises.title: Estimating as in analysis
exercises.description: Show: from $|x - 2| < 1$ it follows that $|x^2 - 4| < 5|x - 2|$. How small must $|x - 2|$ be to guarantee $|x^2 - 4| < 0.01$?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
We split $x^2 - 4 = (x - 2)(x + 2)$ and bound the second factor using the assumption.

Step 2: Bound the factor
$|x - 2| < 1 \Rightarrow 1 < x < 3 \Rightarrow 3 < x + 2 < 5$, so $|x + 2| < 5$.

Step 3: Estimate
$|x^2 - 4| = |x - 2|\,|x + 2| < 5\,|x - 2|$. $\square$

Step 4: Choosing the bound
We additionally require $5|x - 2| \le 0.01$, i.e. $|x - 2| \le 0.002$.

Step 5: Answer
From $|x - 2| < \min\{1;\, 0.002\} = 0.002$ it follows that $|x^2 - 4| < 0.01$.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
Two conditions (here $|x - 2| < 1$ and $|x - 2| \le 0.002$) are combined using the minimum. This is the pattern of the $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ proof.

exercises.title: Radical inequality
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
The domain is $x \ge -2$. Then cases by the sign of $x$, since squaring is only allowed for non-negative sides.

Step 2: Case $-2 \le x < 0$
The left side is $\ge 0$, the right side negative: the inequality always holds. Solution: $[-2, 0)$.

Step 3: Case $x \ge 0$
Both sides non-negative, squaring allowed: $x + 2 > x^2 \iff x^2 - x - 2 < 0 \iff (x - 2)(x + 1) < 0 \iff -1 < x < 2$. With $x \ge 0$: $[0, 2)$.

Step 4: Union
$L = [-2, 2)$.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
Squaring an inequality is only an equivalence when both sides are non-negative. Hence the case distinction.

exercises.title: Absolute value with a square
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$|u| < 3$ means $-3 < u < 3$ with $u = x^2 - 4$.

Step 2: Double inequality
$-3 < x^2 - 4 < 3 \iff 1 < x^2 < 7$.

Step 3: Taking roots
$x^2 > 1 \iff |x| > 1$ and $x^2 < 7 \iff |x| < \sqrt{7}$. So $1 < |x| < \sqrt{7}$.

Step 4: Solution set
$L = (-\sqrt{7}, -1) \cup (1, \sqrt{7})$.

Step 5: Check
$x = 2$: $|0| < 3$ ✓. $x = 0$: $|-4| = 4 < 3$ ✗ – $0$ lies between $-1$ and $1$ and is rightly missing.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
The $|x| > 1$ turns one region into two. Splitting into single inequalities avoids mistakes.

exercises.title: Comparing tariffs
exercises.description: Tariff A costs a base fee of $10\,\text{€}$ plus $0.05\,\text{€}$ per minute. Tariff B has no base fee but costs $0.15\,\text{€}$ per minute. a) From how many minutes on is A cheaper? b) How many minutes are possible with A on a budget of at most $20\,\text{€}$?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
We express the costs as terms in the number of minutes $m$ and solve inequalities.

Step 2: a) Setup
A cheaper: $10 + 0.05m < 0.15m$.

Step 3: a) Solve
$10 < 0.10m \Rightarrow m > 100$.

Step 4: a) Answer
A is cheaper for more than $100$ minutes. At exactly $100$ minutes both cost $15\,\text{€}$.

Step 5: b)
$10 + 0.05m \le 20 \Rightarrow m \le 200$. At most $200$ minutes.

Step 6: Takeaway: What to remember
In word problems interpret the result: the endpoint $m = 100$ is the tie, no longer “cheaper”.
